subject: Commit smoothing and throughput warranty for Dedicated migration
messages:
From: Emily Chan <emily@scalespark.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-08T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Commit smoothing & throughput warranty questions

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the deck today — the migration path from Hosted -> Dedicated is shaping up well. A couple of follow-ups from our side as we prepare finance/legal:

- Conversion credits: you mentioned a conversion allowance tied to our Hosted spend. Can you confirm how credits amortize across a 12-month reserved commit? Are they front-loaded, pro-rated, or applied as a monthly true-up?
- Bridge months: ScaleSpark ramps over Q1 and would prefer 3 bridge months where we keep Hosted consumption while Dedicated capacity is provisioned. Will those bridge months be covered by credits or billed normally?
- Throughput warranty: we need a p95 throughput commitment (tokens/sec) across a 4-GPU equivalent pool with a beta batch profile (avg seq 256). We're looking for clarity on how Redwood measures throughput and what the remedy is if you miss the target.

We can share our projected token curves but wanted the commercial mechanics first so legal can draft. Looping in our procurement (cc'd separately if needed).

Appreciate the quick clarification — Emily
Emily Chan
Director of ML Ops, ScaleSpark, Inc.
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Chan <emily@scalespark.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-08T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Commit smoothing & throughput warranty questions

Hi Emily — great to hear, and thanks for the detailed ask. Short answers up front, details below.

- Conversion credits: we apply conversion credits as a monthly offset against invoice until the credit pool is exhausted (i.e., prorated over the first N months unless you elect a front-loaded drawdown). We can model either approach; many customers pick a 6–12 month smoothing to avoid big first-month true-ups.
- Bridge months: we can treat bridge months as credits (up to an agreed cap) rather than direct billing, provided we receive a signed committed capacity agreement that starts within the bridge period.
- Throughput warranty: Redwood can commit to a throughput SLO defined as sustained tokens/sec for the specified GPU-equivalent pool under the agreed batch profile. Remedy is a service credit tier (percentage back against committed spend) rather than cash refunds. We publish measurement methodology in the term sheet.

Marcus — can you confirm the sizing we discussed (4x A100-equivalent GPUs, baseline 200k tokens/sec sustained at avg seq 256, p95 latency target ~150ms for 1k token responses) and attach a first-pass amortization schedule?

Emily — I'll attach a short term sheet and a sizing worksheet for your procurement to route. If this looks good I'll ask legal to prepare redlines to capture the bridge-month credit language.

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: throughput-warranty-term-sheet.pdf (pdf)]
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Emily Chan <emily@scalespark.com>
Date: 2026-11-09T08:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Commit smoothing & throughput warranty questions

Folks — attaching the sizing/workbook and a proposed credit amortization table. High level notes:

- Sizing assumptions: 4x A100-eq (single tenant pool). Workload mix: 70% chat (avg seq 128), 30% batch prompts (avg seq 512). Using our runtime benchmarks, that maps to sustained throughput ~180–220k tokens/sec depending on burst allowance.
- Measurement: throughput measured at the tenant egress point over 5m rolling windows; p95 latency computed on requests <=1k tokens. We'll include the telemetry hooks in the Console for transparency.
- Conversion credit structure (proposal): total conversion credit = Hosted spend * 0.35 (example). Apply as monthly offsets over 9 months by default. Option to front-load first 3 months at 60% of credit pool if ScaleSpark prefers earlier relief.
- Bridge months: proposed 3 bridge months covered up to $X (line-item in workbook). If usage exceeds cap, excess billed at Hosted rates.
- Remedies: failing the throughput warranty triggers a tiered service credit: 5% of committed monthly fee for minor misses, 15% for sustained (>48h) shortfalls, subject to force majeure carve-outs.

Attachment: commit-smoothing-proposal.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Happy to run the workbook with your exact monthly token curve — Emily, if you drop the projected tokens/month and peak concurrency, I can produce a month-by-month invoice projection showing credits applied.

— Marcus

Thanks both — the proposal looks reasonable from commercial. A couple of small asks before procurement signs:

1) Can you add explicit language in the order form: ‘Bridge months are applied as conversion credit up to the agreed cap and will not be billed separately so long as the committed capacity agreement is signed by the start of month 2.’ That avoids ambiguity for our CFO.
2) For the throughput warranty, can Redwood add a short example calculation in the term sheet showing how p95 throughput is derived from the telemetry data (helps our SREs validate).
3) We'll take the 9-month smoothing as the default, but reserve the right to elect front-loading (first 3 months at 60%) within 14 days of signing.

If you can send a clean order form with those three bullets captured, I'll push to legal and procurement.

Attaching: procurement-statement-of-work.pdf (we'll attach a redline once we receive the order form).

Emily
